_comment: Files this repo VENDORS from other repos, pinned to a tag + sha256.
Do not edit the vendored files by hand -- they are overwritten. Change them upstream, release, repin.
python tools/sync_assets.py            fetch at the pinned tag and verify
python tools/sync_assets.py --offline  local hash check only, no network
python tools/sync_assets.py --update   repin to upstream's newest release tag
python tools/sync_assets.py --check    CI gate (see the script's header for the two severities)
WHY THIS EXISTS. The editor used to hand-maintain every node definition in src/nodes-*.js. That
covered 211 of Ess's 720 public functions and drifted further behind on every Ess release, because
nothing connected the two repos. Ess now generates the node contract from its own source, so the
definitions can be pinned like any other dependency instead of retyped.
THE HAND-WRITTEN NODES ARE NOT REPLACED. They win wherever they exist -- see src/essgen-dedupe.js.
Several of them encode things a generated node structurally cannot, like the validated hotkey and
faction combo boxes that make an invalid value unreachable rather than merely undocumented. The
vendored set fills the ~500 functions that had no node at all.
PIN NOTE: v0.5.0 is the first Ess release to contain api/ess-nodes.generated.js. Until that release is
published, `--offline` is the check that works -- it verifies the local copy against the sha256 below,
which is the half that catches hand-edits and is the reason the pin exists at all. A networked fetch
will start succeeding once the tag is up, with no change needed here.

assets.why: Every public Ess function as a litegraph node type, generated by build/nodes.py from ess.json (what EXISTS, parsed from src/) plus api/nodes.overlay.json (hand-authored beginner descriptions, validated against ess.json so it can never describe a function or parameter that is not real). Registers under the essgen/ prefix so it cannot collide with this repo's own ess/ nodes. Shipped as a script rather than consumed from api/nodes.json because fetch() is blocked on a file:// page and a <script> tag is not -- this editor is meant to work by double-clicking index.html.
